messages.subject: Stan and Big Data
parts:
HI All,

I have two questions regarding Big Data and rstan

1) I am running a simple logit regression (not displayed), and am trying to generate a linear predictor for a new data.frame with 3,091,493 rows in the generated quantities block. The model runs fine, but crashes upon generated quantities. Am I misusing the purpose of the block? i.e.


generated quantities {                        // posterior linear predictor for population table
  
  vector[N_pops] eta[N_waves];
  
  for (w in 1:N_waves) {
    eta[w] = 

beta_stat_age[pops_age]+
beta_stat_gender[pops_gender]+
beta_stat_friend_count[pops_friend_count]+
beta_stat_l28[pops_l28]+
beta_stat_country[pops_country]+
beta_stat_tenure[pops_tenure]+
beta_stat_time_spent[pops_time_spent]+
beta_stat_post_sessions[pops_post_sessions]
;
  }
  }


2) I am trying to run a very large logistic regression model with some random effects, and two very large matrices of linear predictors drawn from N~(0, var), with 13,024 predictors each (model attached). I can get the model to run, but barely (for example, init='random' fails due to memory). Is such a problem too big for stan, or does it make sense to go down routes of sparse matrix representations, which I know are possible now with stan?

Many thanks,
Tobi

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Stan and Big Data
parts:
On Thursday, March 23, 2017 at 12:08:14 PM UTC-4, Tobias Konitzer wrote:
1) I am running a simple logit regression (not displayed), and am trying to generate a linear predictor for a new data.frame with 3,091,493 rows in the generated quantities block. The model runs fine, but crashes upon generated quantities. Am I misusing the purpose of the block? i.e.

It looks OK at first glance. What is the error message? Your model block should change the likelihood from

  gender ~ bernoulli(inv_logit(eta));

to

  gender ~ bernoulli_logit(eta);

for numerical stability.

2) I am trying to run a very large logistic regression model with some random effects, and two very large matrices of linear predictors drawn from N~(0, var), with 13,024 predictors each (model attached). I can get the model to run, but barely (for example, init='random' fails due to memory). Is such a problem too big for stan, or does it make sense to go down routes of sparse matrix representations, which I know are possible now with stan?

The stan_glmer() function in the stanarm package represents such models in the same way that lme4 does, i.e.

eta = X * beta + Z * b

where the Z matrix is sparse and the X matrix is dense by default. There is a sparse = TRUE option to encode X as sparse, but sparse matrix multiplication by a vector in Stan is very slow (it is really only good for the case where RAM binds before patience). Moreover, it is usually better to specify QR = TRUE to reparameterize the model as

eta = Q * R * beta + Z * b = Q * theta + Z * b

where theta = R * beta and stan_glmer() automatically recovers the posterior distribution of beta by pre-multiplying each draw of theta by R^{-1}. However, in that case Q is dense even if X has a lot of zeros.

If you need the posterior predictive distribution or the posterior distribution of eta, you can obtain that using posterior_predict() or posterior_linpred() (possibly with transform = TRUE to get the posterior distribution mu) so you don't have to generate such things in the generated quantities block.

Ben


Ben
